subject: Post-call recap + pilot proposal: Lexicon Health long-history notes
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@lexiconhealth.com>, legal@lexiconhealth.com
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + pilot proposal: Lexicon Health long-history notes

Hi Alicia — great to meet today. Thanks for walking us through the use case and sample note types (ED visits, discharge summaries, multidisciplinary notes). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same picture:

- What you said: long patient histories (20–100 pages) are core to the flavor of reasoning you need for coding/summarization. You need summaries that preserve clinically-relevant timeline and not drop earlier events. PHI scope: direct identifiers are present, some notes may include scanned PDF snippets until we have ingestion parity.
- Main risks you flagged: truncation of critical context, hallucination of dates/medications when prompts crop, and strict auditability for downstream clinical reviewers.

Our proposed pilot (4 weeks, goal: evaluate model fit + quality regressions):
1) Dataset: you provide a redacted sample set (we suggest ~250 multi-section notes) — we can accept pseudonymized JSONL.
2) Benchmarks: we will run 3 model variants (open Llama-70B-8k-quant, Llama-70B-64k-quant, and a dense 34B with extended KV) across a consistent prompt set you approve. See attached benchmark plan and prompt set link.
3) Metrics: extractive recall for key events, timeline fidelity (custom rubric), and summarization hallucination rate. We'll include token/latency cost and a basic SLA suggestion.
4) Delivery: weekly checkpoints (notes + sample outputs) and a final summary with model recommendations and a small production run (10k tokens/day) to validate perf.

Attachments sent with this email: pilot_sow_draft.pdf (SOW template), redwood_longcontext_benchmarks_v1.csv (example metrics we'll capture), lexicon_sample_notes.jsonl (placeholder format).

Questions / asks for you before we kick off:
- Can Lexicon share a pseudonymized sample of ~250 notes by next Tuesday (5/18)?
- Is there an existing NDA or security questionnaire we should route to your legal team?
- Any redline constraints for PHI storage/region?

If agreeable, next steps: I can schedule a kickoff with our product engineer (Marcus) and evaluation lead (Neha) next week. Proposed windows: May 19–20.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0172

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick clarifications before we commit to the sample share:

1) PHI handling: we can provide a pseudonymized dump (no direct identifiers) but our security team will want to confirm KMS controls and retention windows. Is Redwood able to host pseudonymized data in us-east-1 only and enforce 90-day retention for pilot artifacts?
2) Model choices: you mentioned a 64k-kv variant — can you share a short note on how that variant handles sparse attention for very long documents vs. chunk+summarize approaches? Customers of ours have flagged that summarization fidelity drops when earlier clinical notes are truncated.
3) Commercial: please send a ballpark cost for a 4-week pilot (ingestion, evaluation runs, and a small steady-state inference budget). That will help me justify to procurement.

Also, we prefer to keep legal@cc on all documents. I will try to get the sample data ready by 5/18 but can't promise — may be 5/21 depending on compliance review.

—Alicia
Director of Product, Lexicon Health
alicia@lexiconhealth.com

Folks — forwarding Alicia's reply (below). Two asks from her: region/retention constraints and a short note on the behavior of our extended-KV variant vs chunk+summarize. Also needs a pilot cost estimate for procurement. Can you take the lead on the technical note and SOW tweaks?

My thoughts (high-level):
- For retention/region: yes, we can gate pilot artifacts to us-east-1 only and enforce a 90-day retention policy on the evaluation bucket; legal will want explicit log retention details and KMS key rotation notes. Marcus — can you confirm the default retention flow and produce a one-paragraph answer we can hand to their legal?
- Model behavior: our extended-KV variant (L70-64k-kv) keeps a larger KV cache and uses an attention kernel optimized for long sequences; it's still subject to windowing but preserves earlier segments in the KV to reduce degradation. It's different from chunk+summarize in that it preserves the full prefix during generation (less context loss), but chunking can help in inference cost for ultra-long (>100k tokens). Suggest we propose both: primary eval on L70-64k-kv and a secondary workflow that runs chunk+summarize for the top 10% longest notes.

I attached the draft SOW and our initial benchmark CSV. If you want, I can draft the procurement ballpark (high/low) and send to Alicia.

Hi Alicia — thanks, and appreciate the timeline constraints. Quick answers and next steps so procurement/legal can proceed:

1) Data & retention: Yes — we can gate pilot artifacts to us-east-1 and apply a 90-day retention policy. We will use a customer-specific KMS key and rotate per our standard 180-day rotation schedule; we will include a one-page KMS/retention summary for your legal team (attached).

2) Model approach note (short): our L70-64k-kv variant extends the KV cache window to retain a larger prefix across decoder steps and uses an attention kernel optimized for contiguous long spans. Practical effect: better preservation of earlier events vs naive truncation. That said, for documents >100k tokens we recommend a hybrid: run an initial indexing pass to extract metadata/timeline events (cheap), then use the 64k-kv model for final summarization. We'll include a one-page technical note for your engineers.

3) Pilot commercial (ballpark, non-binding):
- Setup & ingestion: $6,000 (one-time)
- Evaluation runs & compute: $9,000–$15,000 (depends on model variant runs)
- Monitoring & small production validation (10k tokens/day): $3,500/mo (pro-rated for pilot)
Estimated pilot total: $18k–$24k for 4 weeks (we will refine after we see sample sizes).

4) Proposed kickoff: Tue 5/25 at 10am ET or Wed 5/26 at 2pm ET. Which works for you?

Attachments: pilot_sow_draft.pdf, redwood_longcontext_benchmarks_v1.csv, lexicon_sample_notes.jsonl, redwood_kms_retention_onepager.pdf

If legal needs the one-page KMS summary now, I can send it to legal@lexiconhealth.com directly. Once we lock the kickoff date we'll send a short mutual action plan and the HubSpot deal link (sharing now): https://hubspot.com/deal/LXN-2027-045.
